analysis:
Examined both telemetry-schema revisions, connection-file metadata, the complete supplied patch and surrounding BASE connection lifecycle against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. docs/reference/telemetry-schema.md:92–93 (head) clarifies that an unregistered session, including reconnecting, can drain without claiming coordinator acknowledgment. It adds no telemetry fields or upload path; no concrete disclosure or authorization regression is established.
CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift:53–100 (head patch) extracts transport construction without changing URL-derived TLS selection, WebSocket message limits, ping handling or endpoint path. Lines 136–148 replace inline handshake handling with CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.start and CoordinatorError(terminalState:), introducing a configured handshake deadline. Surrounding BASE lines 104–126 retain per-session teardown, nonce clearing, registration reset, drain/model-replacement failure and writer unbinding; registration still follows transport readiness. These interactions matter to TB-002 and T-053/TB-011, while transport confidentiality remains relevant to A-001/A-008. No supplied change directly alters inference encryption, cache isolation (T-041), attestation evidence, billing or privileged-helper authority.
Integration must inspect the new handshake helper, handshakeTimeout configuration and terminal-state mapping: they are not supplied here. Verify exactly-once continuation completion under timeout/cancellation/readiness races, transport cancellation on failure, atomic installation of the persistent handler before readiness returns, and continued forwarding of failed/waiting/cancelled states. Also reconcile the documented reconnect drain semantics with the changed drain implementation in other units. These are unverified changed contracts, not demonstrated vulnerabilities; the missing implementation prevents a firm availability/session-lifecycle conclusion.
